adjudication_records.issue_text: booking.userPrimaryEmail is accessed but not included in the Prisma findFirst query, so it would return undefined with only a fallback preventing a crash

adjudication.rationale: In Prisma, `findFirst({ where, include: {...} })` returns all scalar fields of the `booking` record by default, plus the specified relations in `include`. Since the query does not use `select`, it does not omit scalar fields like `userPrimaryEmail`. Therefore `booking.userPrimaryEmail` would not be undefined due to “not being included” in this query (it could only be undefined if the DB value itself is null/undefined).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendee email dispatch logic is inverted: newly added guests receive AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, while existing attendees get the guests-added notification

Permission logic in addGuests.handler.ts uses `&&` instead of `||`, requiring user to be both admin and owner when the variable name implies OR semantics, incorrectly denying team admins who aren't owners

adjudication.rationale:
In addGuests.handler.ts, the permission flag is computed as:

```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```

This requires the user to be BOTH a team admin AND a team owner. The variable name (`isTeamAdminOrOwner`) implies OR semantics, and the subsequent authorization check (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)`) will deny access to team admins who are not owners. That’s a concrete logic defect visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist comparison in addGuests.handler.ts:75-80 is case-asymmetric: blacklist is lowercased but guest emails are not, allowing emails with different casing to bypass the filter
Server-side schema ZAddGuestsInputSchema doesn't enforce uniqueness within the input array, so duplicate emails can be submitted directly to the API and both inserted
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying problem: the input list is not deduplicated/validated for uniqueness, so repeated emails in the request can pass through and result in duplicate attendee rows being inserted (e.g., via createMany).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate detection in addGuests.handler.ts:82-87 is case-sensitive (`guest === attendee.email`), allowing the same person to be added twice with different email casing

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed with `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`, both of which are case-sensitive string comparisons. Since incoming `guests` are not normalized (e.g., `toLowerCase()`), an existing attendee `alice@example.com` would not be detected as a duplicate if the user submits `Alice@Example.com`, allowing duplicate attendees differing only by casing. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Organizer's own email is not excluded from guest additions; since the organizer is `booking.user` not an attendee, adding their email creates a duplicate attendee entry

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `uniqueGuests` only filters out emails already present in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails. It does not exclude the organizer’s email (`organizer.email` / `booking.userPrimaryEmail`) or `booking.user` in any way. Since the organizer is represented separately as `evt.organizer` and is not necessarily included in `booking.attendees`, submitting the organizer’s email as a guest will pass the filter and be inserted via `attendees.createMany`, resulting in the organizer being added as an attendee (duplicating the person in the event as both organizer and attendee).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No check for past or cancelled bookings; guests can be added to bookings that have already ended or are cancelled, which is illogical and could spam attendees

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation/handler (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`) only checks that the booking exists and that the caller is an admin/owner, organizer, or attendee. It does not check any booking state (e.g., cancelled) or time (e.g., `endTime` in the past) before updating attendees and sending emails (`sendAddGuestsEmails`). Since the mutation operates solely on `bookingId`, it will allow adding guests (and trigger notifications) for bookings regardless of whether they are already ended or cancelled, if such bookings still exist in the DB.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No enforcement of seat limits for seat-based event types; `seatsPerTimeSlot` is read but never compared against current attendee count plus new guests, allowing seat capacity to be exceeded

adjudication.rationale: Real issue introduced in `addGuests.handler.ts`: it unconditionally appends new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` without any check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (or current attendee count). Although `seatsPerTimeSlot` is carried into the constructed `evt` (`evt.seatsPerTimeSlot = booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot`), it is never enforced before persisting new guests, so a seat-limited/seat-based event booking can exceed its capacity by adding more guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No user-visible feedback when some guests are silently filtered out; the response always says 'Guests added' even when some entries were skipped, leaving the user unaware of what actually happened

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the server filters the requested `guests` into `uniqueGuests` by removing emails that already exist in `booking.attendees` and any `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. If `uniqueGuests.length > 0`, it proceeds to create only those attendees, but it always returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` and the client always shows `showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")` on success. There is no response payload indicating which emails were actually added vs skipped, so if some entries were filtered out (already-attendee or blacklisted) while others were added, the user receives success feedback that implies all were added. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` in email-manager.ts:533-541 is case-sensitive, causing attendees with differing email casing to receive the wrong email template
Hardcoded English tooltip text 'Remove email' in MultiEmail.tsx:62 instead of using `t(...)`, so non-English users will see untranslated English text

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the Tooltip is rendered with a hardcoded string: `<Tooltip content="Remove email">` (around line 62 in the diff). The component already uses `useLocale()` and `t(...)` for other UI text (e.g., `add_another`), so this introduces an untranslated English string that will appear for non-English locales.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `isInvalidEmail` in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:50-58 is never cleared when the user edits an email, leaving stale error UI visible even after the input is corrected

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `safeParse(multiEmailValue)` fails in `handleAdd()`, but it is only cleared in the Cancel button handler (and indirectly on success by closing/resetting). The `MultiEmail` component updates `multiEmailValue` via `setMultiEmailValue` without also resetting `isInvalidEmail`, so the error message can remain visible even after the user corrects the emails until they cancel or submit successfully.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `handleAdd` in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:41-44 silently returns with no user feedback when `multiEmailValue.length === 0`, providing no error message or disabled button for empty input

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, `handleAdd` does `if (multiEmailValue.length === 0) { return; }` with no toast/message/state update. `multiEmailValue` can become `[]` because `MultiEmail` allows removing an entry via `splice(index, 1)`; if the last entry is removed, the footer still renders the "Add" button, and clicking it will do nothing with no feedback. This is a verifiable UX/correctness issue in the diff.

matched_golden_ids: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same underlying problem: initializing the emails state as `[""]` introduces an artificial empty entry on open, which can lead to problematic/invalid empty values and inconsistent behavior. The golden suggests using `[]` and handling the empty state in the component; the candidate describes the negative effects of `[""]`, aligning with that concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests added for any of the new code, including addGuestsHandler (permission paths, duplicate filtering, blacklist, seat limits, past-booking rejection), email templates, or AddGuestsDialog validation flow

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new functionality (AddGuestsDialog UI, MultiEmail component, new TRPC addGuests endpoint/handler, and new email templates plus sendAddGuestsEmails) but does not add or modify any test files. This is directly verifiable from the changes shown. While the finding lists specific scenarios (permissions, duplicates/blacklist, etc.) that are suggestions for what to test, the core issue—no tests added for the new code paths—is present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send failures in addGuests.handler.ts:155-159 are swallowed with `console.log` with no error details, making failures invisible in production while showing success to the user

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the email sending is wrapped in a `try/catch` that catches all errors and only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging the actual `err` or reporting it. After the catch, the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`, so the client mutation will resolve successfully (showing the success toast) even if `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` failed. This makes email-send failures both non-actionable (no error details) and hidden from the user.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission check uses AND (&&) instead of OR in isTeamAdminOrOwner, requiring the user to be both admin and owner simultaneously, denying access to most team-based bookings

adjudication.rationale:
In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the permission flag is computed as:
```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```
Using `&&` requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner simultaneously. Given the variable name `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and the subsequent check:
```ts
if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;
```
this will deny access to legitimate users who are only admins or only owners, which is a real correctness/authorization bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Original unfiltered guests array passed to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of uniqueGuests, causing existing attendees to incorrectly receive AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the server computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails that already exist in `booking.attendees` (and blacklisted ones), and only those `uniqueGuests` are actually persisted via `createMany`. However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the original unfiltered `guests` array. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the logic checks `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` to decide which template to send; therefore if the input included an existing attendee email (or otherwise filtered-out email), that existing attendee could be treated as a “new guest” for email purposes and receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Passing `uniqueGuests` would avoid this mismatch. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No server-side deduplication within the guests input array in ZAddGuestsInputSchema, allowing duplicate emails that could cause database constraint violations or silent duplicate creation

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: the server-side input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness. In `addGuestsHandler`, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted ones, but it does not deduplicate duplicates within the incoming `guests` array itself. So a request like `guests: ["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` (when not already an attendee) will produce duplicate entries in `guestsFullDetails` and attempt to `createMany` them, which can lead to DB constraint errors if a uniqueness constraint exists (e.g., per booking+email) or create duplicate attendee rows if not.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isInvalidEmail state in AddGuestsDialog.tsx is never reset on success or dialog reopen, causing stale error messages to reappear when the dialog is reopened

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when validation fails in `handleAdd`, but it is not reset in the mutation `onSuccess` callback (which only closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue`). The dialog component is always mounted (rendered in BookingListItem) and only toggles `open`, so reopening the dialog will retain the previous `isInvalidEmail` state and can show the error message again. It is only reset on the Cancel button path, not on success or on dialog reopen.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts uses && instead of || in team admin/owner check, requiring user to be both admin and owner instead of either

adjudication.rationale:
In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the permission flag is computed as:
```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```
Despite the variable name implying “admin OR owner”, the use of `&&` requires the user to satisfy both predicates. If admin and owner are distinct roles (as the function names suggest), this will incorrectly deny access to team admins who are not also owners (and vice versa), making the subsequent permission gate overly restrictive. Using `||` would match the intended semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Booking data including organizer OAuth credentials is loaded before the authorization check, exposing sensitive data to any authenticated user

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking is fetched with `include: { user: { include: { credentials: true }}}` before the permission check. However, those credentials are never returned to the caller, logged, or otherwise used (the code later calls `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, not `booking.user.credentials`). If the user is unauthorized, the handler throws `TRPCError` without including booking data. So while this is an unnecessary/overbroad DB read, the diff does not verifiably “expose sensitive data to any authenticated user” as claimed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guests array in addGuests.schema.ts has no upper bound, allowing thousands of emails in a single request

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`, the input schema defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` (or other size constraint). This means a single `addGuests` mutation request can include an arbitrarily large array (e.g., thousands of emails), which is directly permitted by the validation in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TOCTOU race condition on attendee uniqueness with no DB-level unique constraint on BookingAttendee(booking_id, email)

adjudication.rationale: The handler does a read (`findFirst` + in-memory filter of existing attendee emails) and then a write (`booking.update` with `attendees.createMany`), which is a classic check-then-insert pattern and could race under concurrent requests. However, the proposed finding specifically asserts there is “no DB-level unique constraint on (booking_id, email)”. The diff does not show the Prisma schema/migration for `BookingAttendee`, so the absence of such a constraint is not verifiable from this change. If a unique constraint exists, the DB would prevent duplicates (the second insert would fail).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitivity inconsistency in email comparison — blacklist comparison lowercases but existing-attendee comparison is case-sensitive

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` are lowercased (`.map(email => email.toLowerCase())`), but the check uses `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lowercasing `guest`, so `Guest@Example.com` would bypass a blacklist entry `guest@example.com`. Also, the existing-attendee dedupe check is case-sensitive (`guest === attendee.email`), so a differently-cased duplicate email could be added. This is a real correctness issue introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server schema ZAddGuestsInputSchema does not enforce email uniqueness within the request, allowing duplicate emails in input

adjudication.rationale: Real. In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.refine(...)` to enforce uniqueness, so duplicate emails are accepted by the API. The handler (`addGuests.handler.ts`) also does not deduplicate the input array (it only filters out emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails), so duplicates within the same request can pass through to `createMany` and downstream processing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No check on booking status or seat capacity before adding guests, allowing guests on cancelled or full bookings

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addGuestsHandler` (packages/trpc/.../addGuests.handler.ts), the code fetches the booking and then unconditionally `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` for any authorized user. It does not read or validate any booking status/cancellation field, nor does it check capacity-related fields like `eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot` / current attendee count before adding new attendees. As written, it can add guests even if the booking is cancelled or already at/over capacity (if those concepts exist for the event type).

adjudication_records.issue_text: email-manager.ts uses newGuests.includes() inside .map() causing O(attendees × newGuests) performance, should use a Set

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (email-manager.ts), the diff shows `calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)` calling `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` for each attendee. That is indeed O(attendees × newGuests) due to linear search on an array, and using a `Set` would reduce lookup to ~O(1). However, this is a micro-optimization rather than a clear bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the diff; the logic is correct and typical attendee/guest lists are small, so it’s not a verifiable “real problem” in the sense of a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 getTranslation calls per attendee inside map, should batch translations by unique locale

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `attendeesListPromises` maps over `bookingAttendees.attendees` and for each attendee executes `await getTranslation(attendee.locale ?? "en", "common")`. This results in one `getTranslation` call per attendee (an N+1 pattern), even when multiple attendees share the same locale, causing redundant work. This is directly verifiable in the diff and can be improved by caching/batching translations per unique locale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Linear scan of booking.attendees for guest filtering is O(guests × attendees), should build a Set of existing emails once

adjudication.rationale: The diff does perform a nested scan when computing `uniqueGuests`: for each `guest` in `guests`, it calls `booking.attendees.some(...)`, which is O(guests × attendees). However, this is a performance micro-optimization suggestion rather than a clear defect/bug/security/correctness issue introduced by the change. Given typical bounds (guest emails added via UI), a reasonable reviewer would not treat this as a real problem requiring a finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Original guests input passed to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of uniqueGuests, causing existing attendees to receive wrong email type
matched_golden_ids: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying bug: the function determines which email template to send by checking membership in the input guests list while iterating over a broader attendees list, so the wrong set of emails can be sent to existing vs newly added attendees. The candidate frames it as using the wrong guests list (original vs unique), but the core issue is the mismatch between the attendee list iterated and the list used for the includes check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update uses caller's credentials instead of organizer's credentials, which will fail or produce wrong event

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` using an `EventManager` instantiated with the *caller’s* user object and credentials: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] });`. However, `evt.organizer` and `booking.userId` indicate the organizer may be a different user. The handler explicitly allows non-organizers (`isAttendee` true) to call this mutation, so an attendee can trigger a calendar update that will run with the attendee’s connected calendar credentials rather than the organizer’s, which can fail (no access to organizer’s calendar) or update the wrong calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send failure is silently swallowed with console.log instead of console.error, and handler returns success regardless

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the email sending is wrapped in a `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` block. This (1) swallows any exception (no rethrow), (2) logs via `console.log` and does not include the actual `err`, and (3) the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` even if email sending fails. These behaviors are directly verifiable in the diff and match the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: organizer-add-guests-email.ts uses attendees[0].name which may be empty for new guests, producing broken email subject

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the subject template uses `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. In the new add-guests flow (`addGuests.handler.ts`), newly-created guest attendees are explicitly created with `name: ""` (empty string). Since `calEvent.attendees` is built from the booking’s attendees after the update and no ordering guarantee is shown, `attendees[0]` can be a newly added guest with an empty name, yielding an email subject like `Guests Added: ... with  at ...` (broken/missing name).

adjudication_records.issue_text: MultiEmail.tsx uses array index as React key for a mutable reorderable list, causing stale DOM after deletion

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `MultiEmail.tsx` renders `value.map((field, index) => <li key={index}> ...)` and the list is mutable (items can be added/removed). However, each `EmailField` is rendered as a controlled component (`value={field}` and `onChange` updates the array), so the classic “stale DOM/wrong value after deletion” issue is not verifiably present from this diff alone. Also, the list is not reorderable (only push/splice), and any remaining concerns (focus/cursor jump or internal state inside `EmailField`) are speculative because `EmailField`’s implementation is not shown. Thus the proposed finding overstates a non-proven defect based on the visible code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx recreates Zod schema including new Set on every render instead of hoisting to module scope

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is defined inside the component, so it (and its `refine` callback creating a `new Set(...)`) will indeed be recreated on every render. However, this is a minor performance micro-optimization concern, not a clear bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff. The code still validates correctly and the overhead is negligible in typical usage, so a reasonable reviewer would not treat this as a “real problem” requiring a finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission check for isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, requiring a user to be both admin and owner instead of either one, incorrectly denying plain team admins permission to add guests

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass that check. Given the variable name and the subsequent permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)`, a user who is only a team admin (but not an owner) will be denied permission to add guests, which matches the proposed finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw unfiltered guests array instead of uniqueGuests, causing existing attendees to incorrectly receive a full AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the add-guests notification

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the code filters the input `guests` into `uniqueGuests` (excluding emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails) and only creates attendees for `uniqueGuests`. However it then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original, unfiltered `guests` array. In sendAddGuestsEmails, the per-attendee branch uses `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` to decide to send `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. If the input contains an email that is already an attendee (possible when adding a mix of new + existing emails), that existing attendee’s email will be in `guests` and thus will incorrectly match the condition and receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of the add-guests notification. Passing `uniqueGuests` would avoid that.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isInvalidEmail state is never reset to false when validation passes, causing the stale error message to persist even after the user corrects their input and leading to both server error toast and stale validation message being shown simultaneously

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse(multiEmailValue)` fails, but it is never set back to `false` when validation succeeds or when the user edits the email fields. On a later successful validation (`handleAdd` -> `addGuestsMutation.mutate(...)`), the stale `{isInvalidEmail && ...}` error block will still render until the dialog is closed (only Cancel resets it, and onSuccess closes the dialog). This can also coincide with an `onError` toast from the mutation while the stale inline validation error remains visible.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Broken access control allows any attendee to add arbitrary guests, exposing meeting credentials (video call URL, meeting ID, password) and meeting details to third parties without the organizer's consent

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation explicitly authorizes any authenticated user who is an existing booking attendee (`isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((a) => a.email === user.email)`) to add additional guests, with no requirement that the caller is the organizer or team admin/owner. It then updates the booking attendees in DB and calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` where `evt` includes `videoCallData` (meeting URL/ID/password) derived from booking references, and sends emails (`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`) to attendees/guests. Therefore any attendee can add arbitrary email addresses (minus duplicates/blacklist) and cause meeting details/credentials to be distributed to third parties via calendar updates/emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No server-side limit (.max()) on the guests array schema, enabling mass information disclosure and email bombing through a single request

adjudication.rationale: The new server-side input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts) defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` or other size/rate limiting. The handler then `createMany` attendees from that list and triggers `sendAddGuestsEmails`, which will send emails to attendees based on the (potentially large) attendee list. With no enforced upper bound, a single authorized request (organizer/team admin/owner, or even an existing attendee per the permission check) could submit an extremely large `guests` array, leading to excessive DB writes and outbound email volume (email bombing) and sharing event details to many addresses (information disclosure), all directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitivity bypass in email blacklist comparison: blacklist entries are lowercased but guest input is not lowercased before comparison, allowing case variations to evade the blacklist
matched_golden_ids: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same flaw: the blacklist is normalized to lowercase but the guest email input is not, so case-variant emails can bypass the blacklist comparison using includes().

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitivity flaw in attendee deduplication check (guest === attendee.email) allows emails already present as attendees to be re-added under different casing, creating duplicate records

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, existing-attendee filtering is done with a case-sensitive comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. Neither `guest` nor `attendee.email` is normalized (e.g., `toLowerCase()`), while blacklist checking lowercases only the blacklist entries but compares against raw `guest` (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). This makes it possible to re-add an already-present attendee email using different casing (e.g., `Alice@Example.com` vs `alice@example.com`), resulting in duplicate attendee records unless a DB-level constraint prevents it (not shown in the diff).
